also: put it in your piggy bank

terms.gloss: a little box with compartments for keeping money: a money box
evidence: Hor. Ep. 2.1.175: gestit enim nummum in loculōs dēmittere
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a small receptacle with compartments, a coffer or casket”, with Horace’s line of Plautus eager to drop the coin into his box. In the singular loculus is a pocket (see “pocket”). We have found no Latin name for a money box in the shape of a pig; say porcellus fictilis, a clay piglet, if the shape matters.

phrases.latin: gestit enim nummum in loculōs dēmittere
phrases.english: for he can’t wait to drop the coin into his money box

phrases.latin: Nummum in loculōs dēmitte: ita pecūlium tuum crēscet.
phrases.english: Drop the coin in your piggy bank: that way your savings will grow.

phrases.latin: Porcellum fictilem tibi dōnō dedī, ut nummōs condās.
phrases.english: I’ve given you a clay piggy bank to keep your coins in.
